title: Choose the package page's structure
question: Packages live per owner with source history. The visual system stays MatrixKit Neo; this picks the composition of the package page, which also decides how commits and CI runs show what they built.

options.label: Trunk line
options.lineage: gitmatrix's own commit history, versions pinned onto it
options.thesis: Read a package as a stretch of trunk: every version sits on the commit that built it.
options.viewport: Package name, format and pull command up top; below, the source repo's trunk as a vertical rail with each version pinned to its commit and run, gaps left visible; the selected version's files and tags sit in a right column.
options.risk: A package fed by several repos needs a lane per source, which crowds past three sources.

regions.label: trunk rail: commits with version pins + CI dots
selected version: tags, files, size, actions

options.label: Provenance ledger
options.lineage: a publish ledger, one signed row per event
options.thesis: The package page is a ledger: one row per publish, naming version, source repo, commit, run and actor.
options.viewport: Pull command and the latest version up top; then a dense, newest-first ledger of publishes and tag moves, filterable by source and status, with yank and delete on each row.
options.risk: Tag moves and yanks are rows too, so busy packages read long unless filtered.

regions.label: ledger: version · source@commit · run · actor · size · actions

options.label: Lineage
options.lineage: a chain-of-custody diagram drawn from the graph
options.thesis: Lead with the chain of custody: source repo, commit, CI run, version and tags drawn as one live diagram.
options.viewport: The selected version's lineage spans the top half, sources on the left and tags on the right with the pull command on the tag node; a compact version table below re-centers the diagram.
options.risk: The diagram earns its space for trust questions but is overhead on quick visits for the latest version.

regions.label: lineage: repo → commit → run → version → tags
